role.altitude: The welding machine operator keeps reading drawings, choosing and checking consumables, adjusting settings on test pieces, watching welds and judging stops and rejects; hunting for paper work orders, copying counts and parameters onto shift sheets and keying programs in by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the job terminal and reason codes
role.ambitious_version: An operator who scans a job and finds drawing, procedure, consumables and program ready, and whose shift report writes itself.

tasks.short: Check the production schedule for the next job, find the work order and drawing, read blueprints and the welding procedure to determine specifications, and clarify unclear points.

steps.what: Operator checks the production schedule for the next job
Operator finds the work order, drawing and welding procedure for the job
Operator reads blueprints and the welding procedure to determine specifications: joints, weld sizes and sequence
Operator clarifies unclear points with the supervisor or welding engineer

tasks.design: A terminal at the machine shows the planned job sequence from the planning system. Scanning or picking a job opens its work order, the current drawing revision and the welding procedure, instead of finding papers in a folder or at the office. Reading the drawing and clarifying questions stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work orders and drawings were printed and could be out of date.
tasks.enabler_now: Shop-floor terminals linked to planning and drawing systems.
tasks.still_hard: Drawings with missing or conflicting weld symbols.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that a weld in the drawing cannot be reached by the torch.

reach.learn: Whether jobs start on time more often.

evidence.claim: A shop-floor records app or MES with a dashboard replaces the paper schedule sheet.

assumptions: Boundary: understanding the job before setup; setting up is outside.
Input contract for s1 and s2: the planner keeps the job sequence in the planning system, and engineering keeps drawings and welding procedures in the drawing system linked to the item.
Reading and clarifying keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether terminals exist at each machine.
research_questions: Do welds to an outdated drawing stop?

incremental.description: Operator reports wrong or missing documents on the terminal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few jobs per shift; high: many short jobs per shift.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record counts of parts welded and welding parameters, judge the reason for stops and rejects, record operational information with reason codes, check and sign the shift production reports, and compile them for the supervisor.

steps.what: Operator records the count of parts welded on the shift sheet
Operator writes the welding parameters used per batch
Operator judges the reason for each stop and reject
Operator records operational information: stops and rejects with reasons
Operator checks and signs the shift production reports
Shift supervisor compiles the shift sheets in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Part counts come from the robot or machine controller into the shop-floor records system, and the welding power source records current, voltage and wire feed per seam, so the operator no longer copies them onto a sheet; manual machines are entered on the terminal. When a machine stops or a part is rejected, the terminal asks for a reason code, and the operator judges the reason. The operator checks and signs the shift report on the terminal, and the supervisor sees a dashboard instead of compiling sheets. Counts are tied to machines, not used to rate operators, and this is agreed with the works council.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shift sheets were written by hand and compiled in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Controller and power-source data feeding shop-floor records.
tasks.still_hard: Older manual machines with no controller data.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing why a weld was rejected.

ambition.what: See rejects per hour during the shift instead of the next day.

tasks.altitude: Much less copying; judging and signing stay.

reach.learn: Whether the dashboard replaces the spreadsheet.

evidence.claim: A welding data system records welding data per seam and per component and passes it to MES or ERP.
A Danish parts maker replaced hand-collected production data with live machine data and reported 5% higher efficiency in the first week.
Machine data tied to an operator login can observe performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: shift production records; quality inspection records are outside.

Input contract for s1 and s2: robot and machine controllers and welding power sources connected to the shop-floor records system, about 80% of machines; manual machines are entered on the terminal; s1 and s2 are priced at that share.
Judging reasons and signing keep their full time; the supervisor's time is outside the operator's savings.
research_questions: Do reject causes get fixed sooner?

incremental.description: Operator corrects wrong machine counts on the terminal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly manual machines; high: 80% connected machines.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up metal type and thickness, look up data charts for consumables, select torch tips, alloys, flux and wire according to metal type and thickness, fetch them and record filler batch numbers.

steps.what: Operator looks up metal type and thickness for the job
Operator looks up data charts for tips, wire, flux and gas
Operator selects torch tips, alloys, flux and wire according to metal type and thickness, and checks them against the material in hand
Operator fetches the consumables from the store
Operator records filler wire batch numbers used

tasks.design: The job on the terminal shows the material and thickness from the work order and the consumables listed in the welding procedure, instead of looking them up on wall charts. Selecting and checking the consumables against the material in hand stays with the operator. Filler wire batch numbers are scanned from the spool label into the job record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Charts hung on the wall and were not linked to jobs.
tasks.enabler_now: Welding procedures linked to jobs on shop-floor terminals.
tasks.still_hard: Material that differs from the drawing.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a delivered plate is not what the order says.

evidence.claim: Standard settings and data live in CAM and tool data libraries; no model is needed.

assumptions: Boundary: choosing consumables for a job; buying them is outside.
Input contract for s2: the welding engineer keeps consumables in each welding procedure in the drawing system, about 80% of jobs; s2 is priced at that share.
Selecting and fetching keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of jobs with a linked procedure.
research_questions: Do welds with the wrong filler fall?

incremental.description: Operator reports mismatches between procedure and material.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: one-off jobs without procedures; high: series work at 80% procedure coverage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter operating instructions into computers by loading the job program, turn and press knobs and buttons to adjust settings on test pieces, start welding machines and watch the first welds, and record the settings used.

steps.what: Operator enters operating instructions into computers: program number and parameters
Operator turns and presses knobs and buttons to adjust welding machines on test pieces
Operator starts the machine and watches the first welds

tasks.design: Scanning the job loads the released welding program and parameters from the program library onto the machine, and the operator confirms them, instead of typing the program number and values. Adjusting on test pieces, starting and watching stay with the operator. The power source records the settings actually used, so the operator only confirms them. No model steers the machine.
tasks.previous_blocker: Programs and values were typed from the job papers.
tasks.enabler_now: Networked welding machines with program libraries.
tasks.still_hard: Fit-up differences that need new settings.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing and seeing that the arc is wrong.

reach.learn: Whether operator changes point to programs needing revision.

evidence.claim: A welding data system records welding data per seam and passes it to MES or ERP.
The Machinery Regulation covers AI-powered safety functions from 20 January 2027; it matters only if a model steers the machine.

assumptions: Boundary: entering, adjusting and starting; welding the series is outside.
Input contract for s1: the welding engineer releases programs to the program library; about 80% of machines are networked; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s4: networked power sources record the settings used.
Adjusting and starting keep their full time.

incremental.description: Operator reports programs that needed adjustment to the welding engineer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older machines without a network; high: 80% networked machines.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
